caption:
Smart TV owners are pointing Claude Code at their TVs to strip out ads, bloatware and tracking.
One developer says Claude removed 25 Xiaomi packages from his parents' TV and wrote a new launcher.
Free projects like cleanyourtv and dumbtv now share the setup, but some people have bricked their TVs.

Would you let an AI agent take over your TV?

Follow @neurafeed.ai for daily AI news.

Source: TechCrunch · Photo: Google

slides.headline: Smart TVs watch what you watch. People are now using *Claude* to rip out the ads and tracking

slides.heading: One prompt, *25 apps gone*
slides.text:
Vibe coded my parents' TV this afternoon!

It was showing a sponsored ad before you could even get to Netflix.

Gave Claude Code the model number, it found the TV on wifi, removed 25 Xiaomi packages and wrote a new launcher.

Looks like an Apple TV now lol

slides.heading: Now there are *free kits* for it
paras: Gathin also made cleanyourtv, a free project that strips bloatware from Android TV and Google TV over Wi-Fi, needs no root access and adds a launcher that looks like Apple TV.
Another developer built dumbtv: "your apps, your HDMI inputs, and nothing else." Setup is pointing an AI agent at the project.
slides.note: Gathin says a few thousand people did the same within two days.

slides.heading: The TV is *faster* too
slides.text: This is how fast the TV moves now that Claude deleted all the BS laggy bloatware it comes with

slides.heading: It can also *brick your TV*
paras: AI agents make mistakes and can disable packages the TV needs. One person bricked an Android TV, and another got stuck halfway through a Fire TV.
Smart TVs use content recognition to identify what is on screen, and that data feeds ads. Safer options include launcher apps like FLauncher.

slides.hook: AI agents are starting to fix the gadgets you already own. Follow to see what people hack next.
